title: Russian missiles hit three Kyiv bridges, killing six, after Putin vows revenge for Crimea
dek: The overnight attack damaged crossings over the Dnipro, cut power, heat and water, and damaged two European embassies. Poland says two Russian missiles and a drone fell on its territory.
author: Declaration Desk
body:
Russian ballistic missiles struck three bridges over the Dnipro river in Kyiv early on Friday, killing at least six people and injuring about 15, according to Ukraine's emergency service as cited in reports, in a large overnight missile and drone attack that came hours after President Vladimir Putin promised retaliation for Ukraine's strikes on the Crimean bridge that would be "far more painful".

Three of those killed were employees of Kyivvodokanal, the city's water utility, according to the Kyiv City Military Administration; earlier official figures put the toll at three. Mayor Vitali Klitschko said the Podilsko-Voskresenskyi, Darnytskyi and Southern (Pivdennyi) bridges were damaged and urged residents not to drive. The bridges carry traffic between the two halves of a city of about 3 million, and the strikes were the heaviest on the river crossings since the war began in 2022, according to reports.

## What happened

Explosions began in Kyiv at about 1.25 am local time (4.55 am IST), and further waves of ballistic missiles, cruise missiles and drones followed between about 3 am and 6.30 am, according to reports. The cruise missiles were launched from Tu-160 strategic bombers, according to reports. Klitschko said a critical infrastructure facility had been damaged; the power company DTEK said some consumers in five Kyiv districts were without electricity, and residents of central districts reported losing heat and water. Fires broke out in residential buildings in the Obolonskyi and Podilskyi districts.

Other cities were also hit. In Kharkiv, a drone struck a hospital, injuring at least four people, Mayor Ihor Terekhov said. Five people were injured in Dnipropetrovsk region, Governor Oleksandr Hanzha said, and one person was wounded when a drone hit a tram in Zaporizhzhia. Oleksandr Vilkul, head of Kryvyi Rih's defence council, said a "massive" drone attack had cut power to boiler houses, water pumping stations and hospitals there. Explosions were also reported in Lviv and Ivano-Frankivsk in the west. Ukraine's air force had not published its count of missiles and drones by early afternoon IST.

Russia's defence ministry said it had intercepted 310 Ukrainian drones overnight, according to reports, and Moscow-installed officials said three people had been killed in occupied eastern Ukraine. Neither side's figures could be independently verified.

## Poland and the embassies

Poland's defence minister, Władysław Kosiniak-Kamysz, later said two Russian missiles, one of them a Kh-101 cruise missile, and a jet-powered drone had fallen at three sites in south-eastern Poland, hurting no one. Prime Minister Donald Tusk called it an "intentional provocation", and NATO said allied jets had been scrambled.

President Volodymyr Zelensky said Russia had fired more than 110 missiles and over 400 drones, "one of the largest attacks" of the war. French Foreign Minister Jean-Noël Barrot said the strikes had damaged the Austrian and Dutch embassies in Kyiv, and France has asked for a UN Security Council meeting, according to reports.

## Background

A road span of the Crimean bridge collapsed after a Ukrainian strike on the night of 17 November, the third Ukrainian attack on the bridge in a week, halting the rail link to the peninsula. Speaking in Shenzhen on Thursday after his meetings with US President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping, Putin said Russia's response "will be far more painful than what (Ukraine) did to the bridge" and that Russia would not negotiate ceasefires on energy or maritime trade, according to reports. The three leaders had issued a joint "Declaration towards Peace" in Shenzhen that day.

In Berlin, President Volodymyr Zelensky met leaders of the European-led Coalition of the Willing, who called on Russia to accept a ceasefire on energy infrastructure and a truce for Black Sea shipping. "If you want to stop war, stop trade with Russia," Zelensky told reporters, according to reports.

## What happens next

Engineers will assess the damaged bridges, which carry much of the capital's cross-river traffic and some utility lines. India, which buys Russian crude and has called for dialogue and diplomacy, has not commented on the latest strikes.
